paper.title: UFO2: The Desktop AgentOS
paper.central_claim: UFO2 is a multiagent 'Desktop AgentOS' for Windows (HostAgent + application-specialized AppAgents, hybrid UIA+vision control detection, a unified GUI-API action layer, retrieval-based continuous knowledge integration, speculative multi-action execution, and a Picture-in-Picture isolated desktop) whose deep OS-level integration yields substantially more robust and efficient desktop automation than prior CUAs, outperforming them by over 10% (Operator by 50% relative) even with GPT-4o.
paper.claim_scope: Windows desktop; Windows Agent Arena (154 tasks) and OSWorld-W (49-task Windows subset of OSWorld); GPT-4o and o1 backbones; module evaluations on small subsets; PiP/AgentOS framing is not evaluated quantitatively.

evidence.quote: We present UFO 2 , a multiagent AgentOS for Windows desktops that elevates CUAs into practical, system-level automation.
evidence.support_explanation: Central system claim.

evidence.quote: Even when paired with general-purpose models like GPT-4o, UFO 2 outperforms dedicated CUAs by over 10%
evidence.support_explanation: Headline performance claim attributed to system-level integration.

evidence.quote: current CUA implementations remain largely conceptual
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap: CUAs optimize grounding/reasoning but not OS-level integration.

evidence.quote: Visual detections with Intersection-over-Union (IoU) greater than 10% against any UIA-derived control are discarded.
evidence.support_explanation: Hybrid control-graph rule: UIA controls first, OmniParser-v2 only for non-overlapping detections.

evidence.quote: If a semantically equivalent API is available, Puppeteer prefers it over GUI automation for reliability and atomicity.
evidence.support_explanation: Unified GUI-API rule: API first when an equivalent exists.

evidence.quote: If an API fails or is unavailable ( e.g. , missing bindings or runtime permission errors), the system gracefully falls back to GUI-based control via simulated clicks or keystrokes.
evidence.support_explanation: Fallback to GUI when API is absent or fails.

evidence.quote: Periodically, these logs are mined offline by a summarization module that distills successful trajectories into reusable Example records.
evidence.support_explanation: Self-experience store from successful trajectories; success is decided by the Task Evaluator (E040).

evidence.quote: Documents are structured as json records with a natural language description in the request field and detailed execution guidance in the guidance field.
evidence.support_explanation: Help-document store format.

evidence.quote: Action Prediction: The AppAgent issues a single LLM query to predict multiple plausible actions under its current context.
evidence.support_explanation: Speculative multi-action step 1.

evidence.quote: Actions are executed in order, halting immediately if any validation fails due to interface change
evidence.support_explanation: Speculative execution step 3 with early exit and replanning, validated by UIA preconditions.

evidence.quote: To ensure fairness, each agent is restricted to a maximum of 30 execution steps per task
evidence.support_explanation: Equal step cap across agents.

evidence.quote: API integrations were selectively implemented for three office applications within OSWorld-W as illustrative examples; no APIs were introduced for the WAA tasks.
evidence.support_explanation: APIs exist only for OSWorld-W office apps.

evidence.quote: Consists of 154 live automation tasks across 15 commonly used Windows applications
evidence.support_explanation: WAA denominator: 154 tasks.

evidence.quote: comprising 49 live tasks across office applications, browser interactions, and file-system operations
evidence.support_explanation: OSWorld-W denominator: 49 tasks (one task = 2.04 points).

evidence.quote: Reported baseline scores in OSWorld differ slightly from prior results focused on Ubuntu due to corrections in verification scripts and alignment with Windows-specific tasks (OSWorld-W).
evidence.support_explanation: Verification scripts were corrected for OSWorld-W; extent not enumerated.
UFO2 (GPT-4o): WAA 27.9, OSWorld-W 28.6.

evidence.quote: Operator | computer-use | 20.8% | 14.3%
evidence.support_explanation: Strongest baseline: Operator, with its own computer-use model.
UFO2-base (UIA only, GUI only, no knowledge): 23.4 / 16.3.
UFO2-base with o1: 25.3 / 16.3.
UIA-only detector row: WAA 23.4 (matches UFO2-base) but OSWorld-W 22.4, not the 16.3 in Table 1 for the same UFO2-base configuration.
Hybrid with GPT-4o: WAA 26.6 (CRR 9.9), OSWorld-W 22.4 (CRR 12.5): no OSWorld-W gain over UIA-only 22.4.
OmniParser-only GPT-4o: WAA 26.6, equal to Hybrid 26.6.
Hybrid with o1: gains over UIA-only 25.3 / 24.5 (+2.6 / +4.1).

evidence.quote: The hybrid method consistently outperforms either UIA-only or OmniParser-only settings, raising the overall success rate and converting up to 9.86% of previously irrecoverable cases into completions.
evidence.support_explanation: Author claim of consistent superiority, contradicted by ties in E022/E023.
GUI-only baseline for the GUI+API study: SR 16.3.
GUI+API with GPT-4o: SR 22.4 (+6.1 = 3 of 49 tasks).

evidence.quote: we focus on the 27 office-related tasks in OSWorld and manually develop 12 APIs
evidence.support_explanation: APIs were hand-written by the authors for the office tasks evaluated.

evidence.quote: We create 34 help documents tailored to benchmark tasks
evidence.support_explanation: Help documents are tailored to the benchmark tasks being scored.

evidence.quote: For subsequent tasks, UFO 2 dynamically retrieves up to three relevant past execution logs
evidence.support_explanation: Self-experience logs come from earlier runs on the same benchmark.
Self-experience with o1: WAA SR falls to 20.8 (from 25.3) while PRR is reported as 13.79.
No-knowledge o1 baseline: 25.3 / 24.5 (the OSWorld-W baseline here is 24.5, not 16.3).
Help-document gain with GPT-4o: +3.2 WAA, +4.1 OSWorld-W (2 tasks).

evidence.quote: Both live help-document retrieval and self-experience summarization yield noticeable gains, reducing planning failures by up to 17.7%.
evidence.support_explanation: Author claim; contradicted for self-experience with o1 on WAA (E031).
Speculative-mode comparison: ACS is computed on a success subset of 30 (WAA) and only 10 (OSWorld-W) tasks.
Speculative with o1: WAA SR 24.7 vs 25.3 single, ACS lower.

evidence.quote: by up to 10% on WAA and an impressive 51.5% on OSWorld-W
evidence.support_explanation: Reported ACS savings, computed on 10 OSWorld-W tasks.

evidence.quote: On the WAA benchmark, more than 62% of failures were attributed to Control Detection Failures
evidence.support_explanation: Failure audit of UFO2-base that motivates the hybrid detector.

evidence.quote: we conducted a detailed manual review of all failure cases for UFO 2 -base (GPT-4o) on both benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Manual failure audit of the base system only.

evidence.quote: It assigns partial scores and synthesizes an overall result: success , partial , or failure .
evidence.support_explanation: Task Evaluator is an LLM judge that also gates which trajectories enter the experience store.

evidence.quote: Across all configurations, the LLM inference phase dominates total latency, averaging around 10 seconds per inference.
evidence.support_explanation: Latency breakdown.

evidence.quote: the fully integrated UFO 2 incurs only an additional 1 second per step for its hybrid control detection pipeline
evidence.support_explanation: Cost of the hybrid detector.

evidence.quote: UFO 2 + Operator achieves higher success rates than running Operator alone, particularly on WAA (26.0% vs. 20.8%)
evidence.support_explanation: Operator as AppAgent under the HostAgent (figure-only result).

evidence.quote: We compare UFO 2 with five representative state-of-the-art CUAs, each leveraging GPT-4o as the inference engine
evidence.support_explanation: Stated protocol, whereas Table 1 lists Operator with its own computer-use model: backbone is not matched.

evidence.quote: Tasks involving LibreOffice (in the Office category of WAA) uniformly yield lower SRs across all evaluated CUAs
evidence.support_explanation: Residual weakness for non-UIA-compliant apps.

evidence.quote: 27.9% and 56.7% of OmniParser-v2 detections are discarded due to overlap with UIA
evidence.support_explanation: Fusion statistics.

evidence.quote: The benchmark environments are hosted on isolated VMs with 8 AMD Ryzen 7 CPU cores and 8 GB of memory
evidence.support_explanation: Evaluation environment stated.

evidence.quote: enabling fully isolated agent execution in parallel with active user workflows
evidence.support_explanation: PiP interface claim (non-disruptive UX).

evidence.quote: Most CUAs drive automation directly on the user’s desktop session, hijacking the real mouse and keyboard.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated third gap (disruptive execution).

evidence.quote: Overall, models with built-in reasoning typically achieve higher success rates (SR)
evidence.support_explanation: Backbone ablation: only two UFO2 configurations with several LLMs, figure-only.

evidence.quote: AWM flexibly applies to both offline and online scenarios
evidence.support_explanation: AWM induces reusable workflows from experience; closest fixed neighbor of the experience-store part, not compared.

evidence.quote: a skill-centric framework that enables agents to self-improve by autonomously synthesizing reusable skills as APIs
evidence.support_explanation: SkillWeaver synthesizes APIs from exploration; UFO2's APIs are hand-written, so the contrast is automation of API acquisition.

evidence.quote: 50.6 on WindowsAgentArena
evidence.support_explanation: Later work reports 50.6 on WindowsAgentArena; used only as current relevance, not for the problem placement.
OSWorld-W baselines: UFO2-base is 16.3 in Tables 1 and 5 but 22.4 (GPT-4o) / 24.5 (o1) in Tables 3, 6 and 7 for the same UIA-only, GUI-only, no-knowledge configuration.
No repeated runs, seeds, intervals or run-to-run variance are reported for any success rate.
No human or ground-truth validation of the LLM Task Evaluator that gates the experience store is reported.
No user study, interference measurement or isolation test is reported for the Picture-in-Picture interface.

No held-out application/task split or decontamination between help documents, experience logs, hand-written APIs and the scored tasks is reported, and the cost of authoring APIs/documents is not given.
No token or monetary cost of LLM calls, or build cost of the knowledge substrate, is reported (latency and step counts only).

signatures.object: Observation and action interface of each AppAgent (control detection + execution backend)
signatures.information: Windows UIA metadata (type, label, bounding box, enabled/visible) plus screenshots; OmniParser-v2 detections only where IoU with UIA controls is <=10%; SoM annotation; AppAgent sees the structured control list and may call registered application APIs.
signatures.operation: Fuse UIA and OmniParser-v2 into one control graph; per step the agent chooses between GUI action and a registered API (API preferred when an equivalent exists, GUI fallback on failure).
signatures.output: Executable GUI event or API call per step.
signatures.conditions: Windows UIA coverage; hand-written APIs exist (only Word/Excel/PowerPoint in OSWorld-W, 12 APIs); vision model needs a GPU VM.
signatures.selection_rule_data: API-first preference rule; IoU threshold 10%; no learned selection.
signatures.persistence: API registry and control detectors are static code.
signatures.failure_boundary: Apps with weak UIA (LibreOffice) remain hard; 62% of UFO2-base failures on WAA are control-detection failures; APIs absent for WAA.

signatures.object: Retrieved knowledge in the AppAgent prompt
signatures.information: Per-app help documents (34 authored for the benchmark tasks; at most one retrieved per task) and summaries of earlier successful executions judged by the LLM Task Evaluator (at most three retrieved).
signatures.operation: Embed and retrieve by task similarity; inject into the prompt (ICL); no parameter update.
signatures.conditions: Prior runs/documents exist for similar tasks.
signatures.selection_rule_data: Successful trajectories are kept; no validation of the evaluator (E056).
signatures.later_use: subsequent tasks of the same benchmark
signatures.claimed_effect: Plan-recovery ratio up to 17.7%; SR gains in most cells (E033) but WAA/o1 self-experience drops to 20.8 (E031).
signatures.failure_boundary: Hand-tailored documents, same-benchmark logs, evaluator reliability unmeasured.

signatures.object: Number of LLM calls per task
signatures.information: One LLM query predicts several (control, operation, rationale) actions; UIA precondition checks (is_enabled, is_visible) before each action.
signatures.operation: Predict a batch, validate each action against UIA, execute sequentially, halt and replan on failure.
signatures.conditions: Actions in the batch must be independent of UI state changes between them.
signatures.claimed_effect: Average steps -10% (WAA) and -51.5% (OSWorld-W) on success subsets of 30 and 10 tasks with SR unchanged to slightly lower.
signatures.failure_boundary: Early exit on layout change; validity of the predicted batch is only checked for control existence, not for semantic correctness.

signatures.object: Multi-agent orchestration and isolation (HostAgent/AppAgent FSM, blackboard, PiP, safeguard)
signatures.information: HostAgent decomposes the instruction and assigns apps; AppAgents act with ReAct loops; shared blackboard; PENDING state for risky actions.
signatures.operation: Centralized decomposition, per-app execution, FSM with CONTINUE/ASSIGN/PENDING/FINISH/FAIL, isolated virtual desktop.
signatures.claimed_effect: Operator as AppAgent under HostAgent: 26.0 vs 20.8 on WAA (figure); no isolation of the HostAgent hierarchy for native AppAgents; no PiP evaluation.

gap.author_gap: CUAs overlook system-level integration: they rely on screenshots and simulated input, ignore accessibility APIs and application APIs, and monopolise the user's desktop (Sec 2.3).
gap.checked_gap: The first two limitations are real and are partly measured by the paper itself (62% of UFO2-base failures on WAA are control-detection failures; LibreOffice weak under UIA). The 'disruptive execution' limitation is argued but not measured (no PiP evaluation, E057). Neighbors Operator, Agent S, OmniAgent, NAVI, UFO are run as baselines; the fixed-set experience neighbors AWM and SkillWeaver are not discussed, and UFO2 hand-writes APIs and documents where SkillWeaver automates API acquisition (E051, E052).

lineage_closest_adjacent.source: UFO (original), NAVI, OmniAgent, Agent S, Operator (paper baselines)
lineage_closest_adjacent.unsolved_for_this_setting: API-level actions, hybrid detection, speculative batching in one system
not compared; UFO2 APIs are hand-written

gap.residue: Which modules carry the gain on held-out apps; how much of the OSWorld-W gain comes from benchmark-tailored APIs/documents; variance of the 49-task measurements.
gap.stakes: Practical Windows desktop automation reliability and latency.
gap.method_response: Add structured OS/app signals (UIA, APIs), fuse with vision where UIA is blind, retrieve knowledge, batch speculative actions, isolate execution.
gap.remaining_gap: Hand-built APIs/docs, same-benchmark knowledge, small subsets, inconsistent baselines, PiP/AgentOS claims unevaluated, LibreOffice and cross-app weakness.
gap.unresolved: Generalization beyond benchmark-tailored knowledge and APIs.
gap.current_relevance: Later UI-TARS-2 reports 50.6 on WindowsAgentArena (fixed ref); used only as context (E053).

expectations.reason: Memory/knowledge gains are shown only on the environments the knowledge was built from.

claims.text: UFO2 outperforms Operator and other CUAs by over 10% (WAA 27.9 vs 20.8; OSWorld-W 28.6 vs 14.3 with GPT-4o).
claims.baseline_control: UFO, NAVI, OmniAgent, Agent S (GPT-4o) and Operator (computer-use model)
claims.selection_vs_test: APIs written for the scored office tasks; help documents tailored to the benchmark; logs from the same benchmark
claims.result_denominator: single runs; one OSWorld-W task = 2.04 points; Operator backbone differs
claims.allowed_conclusion: With author-built knowledge and APIs, UFO2 scores higher than the compared agents on these two benchmarks in single runs; the margin is partly tailored to the test tasks.

claims.text: Even the base system (UIA, GUI-only, no knowledge) beats prior CUAs (23.4 vs 20.8 on WAA).
claims.selection_vs_test: no tailored APIs/docs in the base
claims.result_denominator: WAA: 4 tasks of 154; OSWorld-W base 16.3 vs Operator 14.3: 1 task of 49
claims.allowed_conclusion: Small margins over the best baseline (about 4 WAA tasks, 1 OSWorld-W task) in single runs; the OSWorld-W base value is inconsistent across tables.

claims.text: The hybrid UIA+vision detector consistently outperforms UIA-only or OmniParser-only and recovers up to 9.86% of failures.
claims.result_denominator: CRR 9.9 on WAA; OSWorld-W GPT-4o ties
claims.allowed_conclusion: Hybrid wins in o1 cells (+2.6/+4.1) and WAA GPT-4o (+3.2) but ties OmniParser-only on WAA GPT-4o (26.6 vs 26.6) and UIA-only on OSWorld-W GPT-4o (22.4 vs 22.4); 'consistently' is not supported.

claims.text: GUI+API actions raise completion by over 8% and cut steps.
claims.setting: '27 office-related tasks' stated, but SR values 16.3/22.4/24.5 are k/49 fractions (8, 11, 12 of 49); 12 hand-written APIs
claims.selection_vs_test: APIs written for the same tasks
claims.allowed_conclusion: API shortcuts help on author-prepared tasks by 3-4 tasks; generality of the API set is not shown.

claims.text: Continuous knowledge integration (help docs, self-experience) improves unfamiliar-task handling without retraining.
claims.selection_vs_test: docs tailored to benchmark; logs from the same benchmark
claims.allowed_conclusion: Mostly positive small shifts on the same benchmark; o1 self-experience on WAA lowers SR (25.3 -> 20.8); evaluator unvalidated; no unseen-task test.

claims.text: Speculative multi-action execution cuts steps (up to 51.5%) without harming reliability.
claims.result_denominator: ACS on 30 (WAA) and 10 (OSWorld-W) success-subset tasks; SR 24.7 vs 25.3 for o1 on WAA
claims.allowed_conclusion: Fewer steps on tasks both modes solve, with equal or slightly changed SR; the 51.5% rests on 10 tasks.

claims.text: The PiP interface enables non-disruptive parallel work with the user.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Design described; no measurement or user study.

claims.text: Deep OS integration (AgentOS) is the key driver and a scalable path.
claims.baseline_control: no module-by-module full ablation with matched baselines
claims.allowed_conclusion: Plausible and partially evidenced by small ablations; attribution to the AgentOS framing versus engineering for the benchmarks is unresolved.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On Windows Agent Arena (154 tasks) and a 49-task OSWorld-W subset, single-run execution-checked success of UFO2 (GPT-4o 27.9 / 28.6; o1 30.5 / 32.7) exceeds the compared CUAs (Operator 20.8 / 14.3), with small module-level gains from hybrid detection, hand-written office APIs, tailored documents/logs and speculative batching; the gains are measured on environments the APIs, documents and logs were prepared for.
unresolved: consistent baselines across tables (OSWorld-W base 16.3 vs 22.4/24.5)
assessment.reproduction_note: All numbers are author-reported; nothing was re-run.
assessment.evidence_level_note: 'online': both benchmarks are Windows, the knowledge and APIs are prepared for the scored tasks (EVIDENCE rule 2), so no transfer level is claimed.

G.reason: Concrete system-level bottlenecks (control detection failures measured at 62% of UFO2-base WAA failures, UIA-blind apps, long GUI sequences collapsible into API calls) are tied to design choices and several named agent neighbors are run as baselines; nearest fixed-set experience/API neighbors (AWM, SkillWeaver) are not discussed, and the disruptive-execution gap is not measured.

M.reason: Each module targets a stated failure class with a testable prediction that is checked at least on small subsets (hybrid detector vs UIA-only/OmniParser-only, GUI-only vs GUI+API, with/without knowledge, single vs speculative); API-first routing, IoU fusion and validation rules are explicit. Weakened by a broad system scope, hand-written API dependence, and unmeasured PiP/HostAgent claims.

X.reason: Fusion rule, API registration and preference, retrieval caps (one doc, three logs), FSM states, speculative three-stage procedure, PENDING safeguard, hardware and latency are described and failure boundaries (LibreOffice, cross-app, early exit) are named; the Task Evaluator, API set and prompt details are not fully specified and some configuration values conflict across tables.

E.measurement.reason: Execution-checked online success on WAA (154) and OSWorld-W (49) with benchmark scripts and a stated 30-step cap, but OSWorld-W is a small, script-corrected subset, the Operator comparison uses a different backbone than stated, the same UFO2-base configuration has two different OSWorld-W values across tables, and the LLM Task Evaluator is unvalidated.

E.causality.reason: Four module-level ablations (detectors under one LLM, GUI-only vs GUI+API, knowledge, speculative) give real attribution, but they run on 49-task or smaller success subsets, baselines are inconsistent across tables, hybrid ties in two cells, self-experience lowers one cell, and API/doc effects are confounded with benchmark-specific authoring.

E.holdout.reason: APIs were hand-written for the scored office tasks, help documents were tailored to the benchmark tasks and experience logs come from the same benchmark; no held-out apps or decontamination, and robustness to UI change is claimed without a perturbation test.

E.statistics.reason: Single runs with no variance; OSWorld-W cells move by 2.04 points per task, module ablations differ by 1-4 tasks, ACS savings rest on 10 tasks, and one knowledge cell reverses the expected sign.

E.cost.reason: Reports step counts (ACS), per-stage latency, the extra 1 s for the hybrid detector, hardware and a uniform 30-step cap; token/dollar cost, knowledge-building cost and API/document authoring effort are missing.

status.reason: Full text read on the on-disk re-render (all sections 1-9 present). Figure-only results (Fig 19, 23, 25) are not available in text. The manifest hash does not match the on-disk file (see provenance drift); this does not stop scoring because sections and tables are complete, but the controller must reconcile the pinned hash.

rationale.summary: UFO2 is a large systems paper that integrates Windows UIA, vision-based control detection, a GUI/API Puppeteer, retrieval knowledge and speculative multi-action batching into a HostAgent/AppAgent framework. In single runs on WAA and a 49-task OSWorld-W subset it beats Operator and other CUAs, and module ablations give directionally positive 1-4 task gains. The evidence is weakened by hand-written APIs and documents prepared for the scored tasks, same-benchmark experience logs, inconsistent baselines across tables, tiny subsets, no repeats, and unmeasured PiP and hierarchy claims.
strengths: Honest failure audit that motivates the hybrid detector
Module-level ablations with recovery ratios and cost/latency reporting
Clear fusion, routing, retrieval and validation rules
weaknesses: APIs, documents and logs prepared for the scored benchmark tasks; no held-out apps
OSWorld-W baseline differs across tables (16.3 vs 22.4/24.5); Operator backbone not matched
Hybrid detector ties in two cells; o1 self-experience reduces WAA success
Single runs on 49/154 tasks; PiP and AgentOS claims unmeasured; Task Evaluator unvalidated
